scope: Coalesce overlapping planned-assignment reads and serialize their identical HTTP response once, so reconciliation and request handling can make progress.
behaviors: Concurrent reads of the same snapshot mode perform one load and share one encoded response.
Full and lightweight reads remain independent; at most two response promises are retained.
Once a read finishes, a later read loads fresh data; there is no completed-response cache.
Load and serialization failures reject all joined readers and allow subsequent retries.
The real planned-assignment route preserves Express JSON bytes, content type, content length, ETag, and conditional GET behavior.
Unicode, hostile JSON strings, empty arrays, nested JSON, and bursts of concurrent requests preserve response contents.
The existing authorization, reconciliation writes, target checkpoints, and disabled 15-minute scheduler remain unchanged.

failureModel.staleData: Fresh-read and failure-retry assertions; no TTL cache.
failureModel.mixedModes: Overlapping true/false snapshot requests and route query contract.
failureModel.responseDrift: Real Express baseline comparisons and property tests.
failureModel.duplicateWork: Concurrent burst tests assert one load and shared encoded Buffer.
failureModel.deploymentInterruption: Request a normal stop, wait for terminal target state, preserve checkpoints, then resume the same run after healthy deployment.

setup.git: No commits or resets; preserve concurrent workspace changes and deploy only this task's delta over the current live image.
setup.tests: Existing bounded isolated Compose runner and retention wrapper; existing Node test, fast-check, c8, TypeScript and ESLint tooling.
setup.evidence: Persist concise source evidence and operational deployment/recovery audit only.
